name: Muxarr
description: Bulk-strip unwanted audio and subtitle tracks from your media library by remux (no re-encode, no quality loss), with Sonarr/Radarr integration to keep each title's original language. Dropping spare audio tracks alone often reclaims 10-30% of a file, and a 4GB one still processes in about a minute even on a NAS. Under the hood it uses mkvmerge for Matroska and ffmpeg stream-copy for MP4-family, and validates the remuxed output before replacing the original, so a failed run leaves your source untouched. New imports can be auto-processed via webhook, and per-directory profiles let different folders (anime vs movies, say) follow different rules. Features: - Language priority and per-language track limits (e.g. keep only the best English audio), tuned for quality or smallest size. - Metadata cleanup of encoder/codec junk in track names, applied instantly with mkvpropedit (no remux for metadata-only changes). - Library overview of codecs, resolutions and languages, plus a stats API for dashboards. - Supports Matroska (.mkv, .webm) and MP4-family (.mp4, .m4v). Paths: mount your library at the SAME path your Sonarr/Radarr containers use (e.g. /media). If they differ, add a Path Mapping under Settings > Integrations in Muxarr. Add more /media style mappings for libraries that live on other shares.

paths.name: Media
paths.description: Your media library. Mount this at the SAME container path your Sonarr/Radarr use, or set a Path Mapping in Muxarr. Add more Path entries for libraries on other shares.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID for file permissions (99 = nobody on Unraid).

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID for file permissions (100 = users on Unraid).

variables.name: UMASK
variables.description: Permission mask for files Muxarr writes, e.g. 002 for group-writable libraries.
